4. The petitioners as pre-emptees contested the case by filing written objection denying the allegations and contending amongst others, that the claim for pre-emption is barred by limitation, that there is no cause of action, that on getting the proposal for sale of the case land the pre-emptee petitioners on query came to know from respondent Nos.2-3 that they brought up the pre-emptor respondent from childhood on the death of their mother and gave her in marriage with a Police Officer, that the respondent No.2 had also informed them on 1370 B.S. that the pre-emptor had gifted her inherited portion of land to respondent Nos.2-3, that afterwards the pre-emptee petitioners went to the house of respondent Nos.2-3 wherein they learnt from the pre-emptor herself about the gift and that the price of the case land was fixed in her presence at Tk. 30,000/- and thereafter, deeds dated 03.02.1977 and 08.02.1977 were registered that the petitioners had been possessing the same by mutating their names vide Miscellaneous Case No.1920 of 1979-80 and paying tax on opening a separate khatian and developing the land, that the price of the land had increased in the meantime and so the respondent Nos.2-3 have collusively set up the pre-emptor respondent to file the Miscellaneous Cases to make wrongful gain and so the petitioners prayed for dismissal of the Miscellaneous Cases. 

 8. These pre-emptee petitioners had produced certified copy of a deed dated 05.03.1980 whereby the respondent No.3 had sold .20 acres of land of Case Plot No.2630 to one Mahbub Elahi but the trial court did not mark it 'exhibit' as the pre-emptee allegedly could not legally prove the deed as is evident from the judgment of the trail court. The pre-emptee petitioners have had certified copies of two other deeds being deed No.8204 dated 05.03.1980 whereby the respondent No.2 sold .20 acres of land of Case Plot No.2630 to Mahbub Elahi and deed No. 8206 dated 05.03.1980 whereby; respondent Nos. 4 and 5 sold .20 acres of land of case plot Nos.2630 and 2632 to Mahbub Elahi and also the related khatian but being not advised by their advocates did not adduce those in evidence before the trial court. Though the aforesaid sales from the case plots were effected on 05.03.1980 immediately before the filing of the miscellaneous cases for pre-emption on 16.04.1980 but the pre-emptor has not so far filed any case for pre-emption in respect of sale of those land by her sisters herein respondent Nos.4-5 rather had admitted in cross-examination that she had consented to the sales of her brothers. If the aforesaid three deeds and khatian were produced and considered by the courts the decisions might have been different and in favour of these pre-emptee petitioners. The said deeds being certified copies, the court is to presume the deeds as genuine under Section 79 of the Evidence Act and that the execution of the deeds having not been denied by the respondent Nos.2-5 the same need not be proved by attesting witness as per provision of Section 68 of the Evidence Act. The learned Assistant Judge was wrong in not considering the certified copy of one of the said deeds on the ground of not being proved.
